title: Heterogeneous traffic mirroring with gradual-degradation safety policy
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces a traffic-mirroring controller that supports per-cohort heterogeneous mirroring ratios and an adaptive gradual-degradation safety policy; adds API fields and console UI; includes integration tests and observability; non-breaking for existing rollout configs.
description:
Motivation: We need a safe way to run shadow/mirroring experiments that exercise upstream model variants (or new runtime) without risking production availability. Existing mirror controllers at Redwood assume uniform mirroring ratios and a single global safety budget. This PR introduces a heterogeneous mirroring controller that: 1) allows multiple cohorts (user segments) to receive independently configurable mirror ratios, 2) applies a gradual-degradation safety policy that decays mirrored traffic automatically when signals indicate regression, and 3) exposes per-cohort failure budgets, throttles, and an explicit 'trial window' to limit blast radius.

Design summary: The controller implements an adaptive controller loop (mirroring_controller.go) that subscribes to: rollout config, cohort selectors, and metric signals (latency, error-rate, and quality-regression hooks). Key behaviors: - Mirror assignments are expressed as cohort-level weights (0.0-1.0). - A rolling evaluation window computes a combined "safety score" per cohort using configurable weights for latency, errors, and quality deltas. - When a safety score exceeds the configured threshold, the controller triggers gradual-degradation: a percent-decay policy that reduces mirrored traffic by a configurable step (default 30%) every evaluation period until the cohort returns to safe range or the trial window expires. - If degradation reaches floor (default 1%), the controller triggers an alert and can optionally unmirror the cohort. - The policy includes a recovery hysteresis to avoid flip-flop.

Configuration example (new API fields):
rollout: 
  mirror: 
    cohorts: 
      - name: "beta-users"
        selector: "region==eu and plan==beta"
        initial_ratio: 0.2
        failure_budget: 0.02
        safety_weights: { latency: 0.4, errors: 0.4, quality: 0.2 }
    gradual_degradation: 
      step: 0.3
      period_seconds: 300
      floor_ratio: 0.01
      evaluation_window: 900
      alert_on_floor: true

Operational notes: - This PR wires mirror telemetry into the Console (Traffic Mirror dashboard) with per-cohort charts and the aggregate safety-heat map. - We added a lightweight evaluation endpoint so SREs can simulate policy outcomes against historical traces. - Default behavior is conservative: if no cohort config exists, the controller behaves like the prior uniform mirror with an implicit low default ratio (0.01).

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover the safety-score computation, decay math, and hysteresis. Integration tests (e2e) simulate a three-cohort rollout exercising degrade/recover cycles; these live under e2e/test/traffic_mirror_integration.test.ts and are included in CI. Benchmarks show controller CPU overhead under 50ms per evaluation for up to 10k concurrent cohorts.

Backward compatibility & migration: API additions are additive; agents without cohort configs continue using platform defaults. We added a migration job to populate a conservative cohort for customers relying on global mirror fields.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of controller loop and policy - [x] API and proto changes + model upgrades - [x] Console UI for cohort creation and charts - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmarks and perf microprofile - [x] Documentation (docs/rollouts/traffic-mirroring.md)

Related: ENG-4382 implements the evaluation heuristics; ENG-4410 tracks Console UX work.
